newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market light at $73 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market light at $73 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were slow Thursday following Wednesday's active trading, feedlot sources said.
Light sales were reported at $73.00 per cwt, steady with Wednesday, with about 1,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and 2,000 in Kansas, according to private sources and USDA.
Prices this week advanced $1.00, compared with last week, on continued tight cattle supplies on feedlots that were market ready, the feedlot sources said.

Prices for cattle have been so profitable for owners that they have been pulling cattle ahead by as much as three weeks in attempts to fill a marketing hole created by light placements earlier in the year, market sources said.
Packer demand also was stoked by strong beef prices.
However, ideas that slaughter this week was resupplying beef stocks fueled concern that beef prices were near a top and starting to falter, they said.
USDA estimated cattle slaughter Thursday at 129,000 head, which brought the week-to-date figure to 481,000, up 1.3 percent from a week ago.
